names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 20 februarie, «Sfântul Cuvios Visarion».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 20 Φεβρουαρίου, «Όσιος Βησσαρίων», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 6. јун ст. ст., „Преподобни Висарион“ — Преподобни is the `venerable` this corpus puts in `types` and is stripped, and the heading has nothing else in it, no place and no epithet. `foldchk.py` returns `[('bessarion-of-larissa', 'sr')]`: a fold of two on the bare form, deliberate, the other man a metropolitan of Larissa.

The name as days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 424 gives it, «Виссарион Египетский, пустынник», with the grade «пустынник», the hermit, which this folder already carries in `types` taken off. Measured with the gate's own fold before it was written: 'виссарион египетскии' has no other holder. The day line calls him «чудотворца Египетского» where the name page calls him «Египетский, пустынник»; чудотворец is a rank word in BRIEF-RUSSIAN §6's list and is the `wonderworker` in `types`, so the toponymic is all that is stored. The folder's own kontakion spells him «Висарионе» with one с, which is the page's spelling in the hymn and not in the heading.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 6 июня ст. ст. — «Прп. Виссариона , чудотворца Египетского (IV-V).»

attestations.note: The day's first entry of eight, «Прп. Виссариона , чудотворца Египетского (IV-V).». The Serbian row of this folder already stands on this same 6 June, where the Romanian and the Greek keep him on 20 February, so this calendar agrees with the Serbian and the identification is the day, the Egypt and the wonderworker's grade this folder already carries in `types`. The line's «(IV-V)» sits inside the folder's own floruit of 351 to 450, «late 4th – early 5th century», so nothing of `dates` was touched. The day page prints ONE troparion for him and Hilarion together and a kontakion of his own, and both are added. `life1247` was NOT read, so nothing of his life is touched here. azbyka.ru was not read.

feast.note: Doxologia keeps him twice: its calendar prints him on 20 februarie and again on 6 iunie — «Sfântul Cuvios Visarion». One attestation row per church is the schema, so the row is the day this folder was read from and the second day is recorded here. The 6 iunie page carries the fuller life — the same Bessarion the Great of Egypt, who saw Gerasimus in the desert of the Jordan and died in great old age — and the troparion below is from it. Read 25 September 2026.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 20 februarie — «Sfântul Cuvios Visarion»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 20ής Φεβρουαρίου — «Όσιος Βησσαρίων»
Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 19.06.2026 (6. јун ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Висарион“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. THE DAY WAS CHECKED, FOR THE FOURTH DAY RUNNING, AND IT IS THIS BOOK’S ONLY ONE FOR HIM. doxologia keeps him TWICE, on 20 februarie and again on 6 iunie, and this folder’s `romanian` row carries the 20 February with the second day recorded in its note; saint.gr keeps the 20 February. **This book keeps the 6 June, which is doxologia’s second day and not its row’s day** — each row carries its own day, as the schema intends. `sr-cand.mjs 02-20` prints this book’s own Julian 20 February, which is Leo bishop of Catania and the hieromartyr Sadok, **and does not name him**, so there is no second Serbian day and no note is owed. TWO TEACHERS NEITHER EARLIER BOOK NAMED, AND THEY ARE TWO RECIPROCAL `related` ROWS. This folder’s own life says doxologia «names no monastery and no teacher», and saint.gr names none either. This book names two: „Посетио је светог Герасима на Јордану, и слушао је светог Исидора Пелусиота“. Both are held: `gerasimus-of-the-jordan` (one of eighteen Gerasimuses, told by the river) and `isidore-of-pelusium` (one of eleven Isidores, told by the see). **A visit and a hearing are a relation in the plain sense — the body narrates both, and the page’s own linker matches both display forms, so a row is owed in both directions or the life would carry a link with no row.** Added here and on each of theirs. **„466. године“ REFUSED, ON THE 31 MAY READING, AND IT IS THE AUTHOR’S.** This folder holds `floruit` 351 to 450, display «late 4th – early 5th century», off saint.gr’s «έζησε περί τα τέλη του 4ου και αρχές του 5ου αιώνα», and no `death` at all. This book states one flat, and it falls SIXTEEN YEARS BEYOND the far end of that interval. `dates` is untouched, for three stated reasons: writing `death` 466 beside a `floruit` ending 450 would have the folder assert activity stopping in 450 and a death sixteen years later; replacing the floruit would be overwriting another book’s reading rather than widening it, which is what `philosophos-of-alexandria` was refused on 31 May; and the Greek interval is itself an approximation («περί τα τέλη»), so the two are not commensurable. **Both books agree he lived to deep old age, which is the one thing that could reconcile them, and that is a length of life and no source for a year.** AND THE YEAR IS KEPT AWAY FROM A DEATH VERB IN THE LIFE ON PURPOSE: this folder has no `death`, so `date-audit`’s `stated` reads its prose, and a repose verb beside 466 would have put a refused year into the audit. Measured: `stated` 153, unmoved. `types` untouched — Преподобни is the `venerable` already there, and `hermit` and `wonderworker` are both corroborated by this entry’s mountains and woods and its „велики дар чудотворства“. No `locations`: Egypt is a country. THE FOLD IS DELIBERATE: `foldchk.py` returns `[('bessarion-of-larissa', 'sr')]`, so the bare form makes a fold of two; the heading offers nothing else at all. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Cu curgerile lacrimilor tale ai lucrat pustiul cel neroditor şi cu suspinurile cele dintru adânc ai făcut ostenelile tale însutit roditoare; şi te-ai făcut luminător lumii, strălucind cu minunile, Visarion, părintele nostru. Roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Visarion, Glas 8

english.text: With the streams of thy tears thou didst till the barren desert, and with sighs out of the deep thou didst make thy labours bear fruit a hundredfold; and thou wast made a light to the world, shining with wonders, Bessarion our father. Pray Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Боже отец наших,/ творяй присно с нами по Твоей кротости,/ не отстави милость Твою от нас,/ но молитвами их// в мире управи живот наш.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, «Тропарь преподобных Виссариона и Илариона», глас 4, under «Молитвы» on the day page for 6 июня ст. ст.. It is printed ONCE, for the two of them together, and is the common of venerable fathers in the plural — it names neither man and says only «но молитвами их», by their prayers. Its heading sets it over both, so it is on both folders (BRIEF.md §4).

english.text: O God of our fathers, who dealest ever with us according to Thy gentleness, take not Thy mercy from us, but by their prayers govern our life in peace.

hymns.text: Вышних сил подражав, преподобне,/ образом птиц житие пожил еси,/ временная в забытии положив,/ непрестанным желанием влеком к Небесным добротам Христа Царя,/ дондеже Того достигл еси, Висарионе,// моли непрестанно о всех нас.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, «Кондак преподобного Виссариона», глас 2, under «Молитвы» on the day page for 6 июня ст. ст.. It names him in the vocative, spelling it «Висарионе» with one с where the heading has two, and it is copied as printed. «образом птиц», in the manner of the birds, is the saying about him this folder's own life already carries from the other calendars.

english.text: Emulating the powers on high, O venerable one, thou didst live the life of the birds, laying aside all temporal things in forgetfulness, drawn by unceasing desire to the heavenly beauties of Christ the King, until thou didst attain to Him, O Bessarion: pray thou unceasingly for us all.

floruit.note: saint.gr: «γεννήθηκε στην Αίγυπτο, στην πόλη Μισήρι και έζησε περί τα τέλη του 4ου και αρχές του 5ου αιώνα μ.Χ.». The page gives no year of birth and no year of death.
